boundary_rationale: The unit opens on a plural summons, שִׁמְע֣וּ אֶת הַדָּבָ֗ר (oshb:Jer.10.1, byte), matching “Hear the word which Yahweh speaks to you, house of Israel!” (web:Jer.10.1). A koh-amar onset follows at once, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.10.2, byte), placing the idol mockery of the surrounding verses in Yahweh's own mouth rather than the prophet's. A doxological interjection breaks in mid-polemic, מֵאֵ֥ין כָּמ֖וֹךָ יְהוָ֑ה גָּד֥וֹל (oshb:Jer.10.6, byte) — praise addressed directly to Yahweh — so that idol mockery and praise alternate through the same speech rather than sitting in separate blocks; no additional koh-amar, addressee shift, or discourse imperative interrupts that alternation, so it is read here as one unit rather than divided at these internal turns. It closes on an Aramaic sentence, כִּדְנָה֙ תֵּאמְר֣וּן לְה֔וֹם אֱלָ֣הַיָּ֔א דִּֽי שְׁמַיָּ֥א וְאַרְקָ֖א לָ֣א עֲבַ֑דוּ (oshb:Jer.10.11, byte) — “You shall say this to them: ‘The gods that have not made the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth, and from under the heavens.’” (web:Jer.10.11) — a self-contained Aramaic island inside the surrounding Hebrew, functioning as the refutation formula Israel is told to hand back to the nations; the citation imperative that opens it belongs with the preceding mockery, and the row is cut here because verse 12 opens a distinct hymnic unit in Hebrew rather than continuing this address.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the praise interjections from the surrounding idol mockery into their own row was rejected because no koh-amar onset, addressee shift, or discourse imperative marks a fresh seam between them; the two registers interleave inside the same divine speech.
literature_type_guess: idol polemic with interleaved praise and an embedded refutation formula

boundary_rationale: Where the Aramaic sentence just before it argues from what the nations' gods did not do, this unit pivots to what Yahweh did do: a participial hymn opening, עֹשֵׂ֥ה אֶ֨רֶץ֙ בְּכֹח֔וֹ (oshb:Jer.10.12, byte), matching “God has made the earth by his power.” (web:Jer.10.12). The register shift out of the Aramaic citation formula that closed the previous verse (web:Jer.10.11) into a Hebrew creation doxology marks the edge; nothing internal to verses 12-16 breaks the hymn again. It closes on the name-formula, יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת שְׁמֽוֹ (oshb:Jer.10.16, byte) — “Yahweh of Armies is his name.” (web:Jer.10.16) — the same formula that closes the hymn's twin at Jer.51.15-Jer.51.19, cross-referenced here as texture rather than as the warrant for this edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this hymn into the surrounding polemic as one larger row was rejected because the participial hymn-opening and the shift out of the Aramaic citation formula are a sharper register break than anything inside the polemic itself, and the hymn is a bounded, self-closing unit with its own twin elsewhere in the book.

boundary_rationale: A second-person feminine command opens the unit, אִסְפִּ֥י מֵאֶ֖רֶץ כִּנְעָתֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.10.17, byte), matching “Gather up your wares out of the land, you who live under siege.” (web:Jer.10.17), addressed to the besieged city rather than to the idol-worshippers of the preceding hymn; the same verse carries a ketiv/qere note on the feminine participle naming that addressee (WLC, single-witness), read further below. A koh-amar clause follows at once, כִּֽי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.10.18, byte) — “Behold, I will sling out the inhabitants of the land at this time, and will distress them, that they may feel it.” (web:Jer.10.18) — joined to the command by an explicit because rather than opening a fresh address, so it is held inside the same unit rather than cut into its own row. Verses 19-21 shift, carrying no formula of their own, into a first-person cry of pain and a shepherds' indictment, and verse 22 closes on a report of a commotion out of the north, ק֤וֹל שְׁמוּעָה֙ (oshb:Jer.10.22, byte) — “The voice of news, behold, it comes, and a great commotion out of the north country,” (web:Jer.10.22). Those internal turns do not carry a koh-amar onset, an addressee change, or a discourse imperative of their own, so the whole stretch from the command through the report is held as one unit; the row is cut before verse 23 because that verse turns the address around, from a report about the coming danger to direct prayer speech to Yahweh.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a fresh row at the koh-amar clause in verse 18 was rejected because it is bound to verse 17's command by an explicit causal because rather than by any addressee change, and the unmarked turn into a first-person voice at verse 19 was held on the same ground rather than treated as its own seam.
literature_type_guess: siege announcement with an embedded cry of pain and shepherds' indictment

boundary_rationale: The address turns from a report about the coming danger to direct prayer speech to Yahweh, יָדַ֣עְתִּי יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.10.23, byte), matching “Yahweh, I know that the way of man is not in himself.” (web:Jer.10.23); nothing before this verse addresses Yahweh in the second person. The prayer moves from submission to correction into an imprecation against the nations that devoured Jacob, שְׁפֹ֣ךְ חֲמָתְךָ֗ (oshb:Jer.10.25, byte), matching “Pour out your wrath on the nations that don’t know you,” (web:Jer.10.25), without a new formula or addressee change between the two movements, so both stand as one unit. The unit, and the surrounding narrative frame that opened at Jer.7.1, close together at this verse.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the submission plea in verses 23-24 from the imprecation in verse 25 into separate rows was rejected because both remain addressed to Yahweh in the same first-person prayer voice across the turn from petition to imprecation.

boundary_rationale: A prose-sermon superscription opens the unit, הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָיָ֣ה אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֔הוּ מֵאֵ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.11.1, byte), matching “The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.11.1) — the same header shape that opened the temple sermon at Jer.7.1, here introducing a covenant sermon instead. The commission continues without a break through the summons to hear, “Hear the words of this covenant,” (web:Jer.11.2), and the covenant-curse content it introduces, closing on Jeremiah's own reply to what he has been told to say, וָאַ֥עַן וָאֹמַ֖ר אָמֵ֥ן יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.11.5, byte) — “Amen, Yahweh.” (web:Jer.11.5). The row is cut there because a fresh introduction, Yahweh said to me, reopens address at verse 6 with a new command to proclaim, after Jeremiah's reply has closed this initial exchange.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through the historical recap that follows was rejected because a fresh Yahweh-said-to-me introduction reopens address at verse 6, after Jeremiah's own reply closes the initial commissioning exchange.

boundary_rationale: A fresh narrative introduction opens the unit, וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֵלַ֔י קְרָ֨א (oshb:Jer.11.6, byte) — “Yahweh said to me,” (web:Jer.11.6) — carrying a new command to proclaim in the cities and streets. The content recalls the fathers' disobedience despite Yahweh's own protest, “Obey my voice.” (web:Jer.11.7), and closes on the covenant curse already brought upon them, with the recap running to its close as one address. The row is cut before verse 9 because that verse opens with the same Yahweh-said-to-me formula again, this time turning to a different topic, a conspiracy among the present generation rather than the fathers' history.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this recap into the same row as the conspiracy oracle that follows was rejected because verse 9 repeats the Yahweh-said-to-me introduction with a new subject, the present generation's conspiracy rather than the fathers' history recalled here.

boundary_rationale: The same narrative-introduction formula reopens address with a new subject, וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י נִֽמְצָא קֶ֨שֶׁר֙ (oshb:Jer.11.9, byte) — “Yahweh said to me,” (web:Jer.11.9) — a conspiracy among the present generation rather than the fathers' history just recalled. boundary_rationale: A discourse-frame prohibition opens the unit, וְאַתָּ֗ה אַל תִּתְפַּלֵּל֙ (oshb:Jer.11.14, byte), matching “Therefore don’t pray for this people.” (web:Jer.11.14), addressed to the prophet himself. boundary_rationale: The scene turns to Jeremiah's own first-person account, וַֽיהוָ֥ה הֽוֹדִיעַ֖נִי וָֽאֵדָ֑עָה (oshb:Jer.11.18, byte), matching “Yahweh gave me knowledge of it, and I knew it.” (web:Jer.11.18); nothing before this verse is cast in this voice. boundary_rationale: The speaking voice turns from Jeremiah's own prayer back to Yahweh's, לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ עַל אַנְשֵׁ֣י עֲנָת֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.11.21, byte), matching “Therefore Yahweh says concerning the men of Anathoth, who seek your life,” (web:Jer.11.21), naming the men of Anathoth who threaten the prophet's life. boundary_rationale: A dispute addressed directly to Yahweh opens the unit, צַדִּ֤יק אַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֥י אָרִ֖יב אֵלֶ֑יךָ (oshb:Jer.12.1, byte), matching “You are righteous, Yahweh, when I contend with you;” (web:Jer.12.1) — a new first-person voice against the judgment oracle that closes the previous chapter. The complaint presses the question directly, “Why does the way of the wicked prosper?” (web:Jer.12.1), and continues through the land's mourning and the wicked's own boast that they won't see Jeremiah's latter end. The row is cut before verse 5 because the addressee there turns around: second person switches from naming Yahweh to naming Jeremiah himself, without any formula marking the change.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this unit through Yahweh's reply that follows was rejected because the addressee plainly turns around at verse 5, from Jeremiah speaking to Yahweh to Yahweh speaking to Jeremiah, even though no koh-amar or other formula marks that turn.

boundary_rationale: The addressee turns around without any introducing formula: כִּ֣י אֶת רַגְלִ֥ים רַ֨צְתָּה֙ וַיַּלְא֔וּךָ (oshb:Jer.12.5, byte), matching “If you have run with the footmen, and they have wearied you, then how can you contend with horses?” (web:Jer.12.5), reads as Yahweh's own reply to the complaint just voiced, now naming Jeremiah as the one addressed rather than the one speaking. boundary_rationale: The voice turns again to Yahweh's own first person, now over the land rather than in reply to Jeremiah, עָזַ֨בְתִּי֙ אֶת בֵּיתִ֔י נָטַ֖שְׁתִּי אֶת נַחֲלָתִ֑י (oshb:Jer.12.7, byte), matching “I have forsaken my house. I have cast off my heritage.” (web:Jer.12.7); the referents shift from Jeremiah's brothers and father's house to my house and my heritage. The unit continues through the devastation of the vineyard, “Many shepherds have destroyed my vineyard.” (web:Jer.12.10), and closes on the sown-wheat, reaped-thorns image of exhausted profit. No koh-amar, addressee change, or discourse imperative interrupts verses 7-13 internally, so they stand as one unit; the row is cut before verse 14 because a koh-amar clause there turns the address outward, to the neighboring nations rather than the heritage itself.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Carrying this unit through the judgment on the neighboring nations that follows was rejected because a koh-amar clause at verse 14 turns the address outward, from Yahweh's own heritage to the nations who touch it.

boundary_rationale: A koh-amar clause turns the address outward to the neighboring nations, כֹּ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.12.14, byte), matching “Behold, I will pluck them up from off their land,” (web:Jer.12.14), naming those who touch the heritage just lamented rather than the heritage itself. A promise of compassion for Jacob and a conditional blessing for the neighbors who learn Jacob's ways are folded into the same speech rather than opening fresh units of their own — an operative judgment-oracle reading is kept for the whole four verses, with the restoration content disclosed here rather than given a separate label, since the unit opens and closes on uprooting language and the compassion clause is grammatically subordinate to it. The unit, and the chapter, close on the closing-speech formula, נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.12.17, byte), matching “But if they will not hear, then I will pluck up that nation, plucking up and destroying it,” (web:Jer.12.17); a fresh command opens immediately afterward at web:Jer.13.1, corroborating the close read here.
